problem.summary: 如何评估从预训练卷积神经网络（CNN）中提取的通用特征在多种视觉识别任务中的有效性，而无需针对特定任务进行微调。

motivation.summary: 尽管已有研究表明CNN特征具有强大的泛化能力，但这些研究仅限于少数视觉任务。本文旨在系统性地验证这些“开箱即用”的CNN特征在更广泛、更困难的识别任务上的表现，以证明其作为通用图像表示的潜力。

core_idea.summary: 使用在ImageNet ILSVRC13上预训练的OverFeat网络作为固定的特征提取器，提取其第一个全连接层（4096维）的特征向量，并结合简单的线性分类器（如SVM）来处理多种视觉识别任务，包括图像分类、场景识别、细粒度识别、属性检测和图像检索。

method.summary: 1. 使用预训练的OverFeat网络（大型版本）提取图像特征。2. 将图像调整为221×221像素，提取第22层（第一个全连接层）的4096维特征向量。3. 对特征进行L2归一化。4. 使用线性SVM（分类任务）或L2距离（检索任务）进行分类或匹配。5. 对于增强版本（CNNaug-SVM），采用数据增强技术（如裁剪、旋转、分量幂变换）扩充训练集。

experiments.summary: 在多个数据集上进行了广泛实验：Pascal VOC 2007（图像分类）、MIT-67（场景识别）、CUB 200-2011和Oxford 102 Flowers（细粒度识别）、UIUC 64和H3D（属性检测）、Oxford5k、Paris6k、Sculptures6k、Holidays和UKBench（图像检索）。结果表明，CNN特征在大多数任务上均优于或媲美当时最先进的专用方法。

claims.claim: 从预训练CNN中提取的通用特征（开箱即用）在多种视觉识别任务上表现出色，甚至优于高度调优的专用系统。
简单的线性分类器（如SVM）与CNN特征结合即可获得强大性能，表明特征本身已编码了丰富的语义信息。
通过简单的数据增强技术（如裁剪、旋转、幂变换）可以进一步提升性能。
CNN特征在图像检索任务上，与低内存占用方法相比，也表现出一致的高性能。
CNN特征本身具有一定的姿态不变性和部件感知能力。

limitations.limitation: 实验仅使用了OverFeat网络，未与其他公开的CNN实现（如AlexNet、Caffe）进行系统比较。
未进行目标检测任务的实验（尽管引用了相关工作）。
对于某些特定任务（如雕塑数据集的检索），CNN特征的表现不如某些专用方法。
未探索通过微调CNN来进一步提升性能的可能性（尽管作者承认这可能会带来提升）。

nodes.title: 预训练CNN特征提取
nodes.label: 特征提取器
nodes.summary: 使用在ImageNet ILSVRC13上预训练的OverFeat网络作为固定的特征提取器，从第一个全连接层提取4096维特征向量。
nodes.description: 输入图像被调整为221×221像素，通过OverFeat网络前向传播，提取第22层（第一个全连接层）的输出作为特征表示。该特征向量随后进行L2归一化。

nodes.title: 数据增强
nodes.label: 数据预处理
nodes.summary: 对训练数据进行增强，包括裁剪、旋转和分量幂变换，以扩充训练集并提升模型鲁棒性。
nodes.description: 对于CNNaug-SVM设置，通过添加裁剪和旋转样本，并对特征进行分量幂变换（每个维度取平方）来增强训练数据。

nodes.title: 线性SVM分类器
nodes.label: 分类器
nodes.summary: 使用线性支持向量机（SVM）作为分类器，对提取的CNN特征进行分类。
nodes.description: 对于分类任务，使用线性SVM（通过libsvm或liblinear实现）对L2归一化的4096维特征进行分类。对于多类问题，采用一对一策略。

nodes.title: L2距离检索
nodes.label: 检索方法
nodes.summary: 对于图像检索任务，使用L2距离度量查询图像与数据库图像特征之间的相似性。
nodes.description: 在图像检索中，通过计算查询图像特征与数据库图像特征之间的L2距离进行匹配。对于空间搜索，采用多尺度子块提取和最小距离聚合策略。

nodes.title: 多任务评估
nodes.label: 评估框架
nodes.summary: 在多种视觉识别任务上评估CNN特征的通用性，包括图像分类、场景识别、细粒度识别、属性检测和图像检索。
nodes.description: 系统性地在多个公开数据集上评估CNN特征，任务逐渐偏离原始训练任务（ImageNet分类），以测试特征的泛化能力。

edges.label: 特征增强
edges.description: 提取的CNN特征经过数据增强处理以提升分类性能。

edges.label: 特征输入
edges.description: 提取的CNN特征作为输入提供给线性SVM分类器。

edges.label: 特征输入
edges.description: 提取的CNN特征作为输入用于计算L2距离进行检索。

edges.label: 增强特征输入
edges.description: 经过数据增强的特征作为输入提供给线性SVM分类器。

edges.label: 分类结果
edges.description: SVM分类器的输出用于在分类任务上进行评估。

edges.label: 检索结果
edges.description: 基于L2距离的检索结果用于在检索任务上进行评估。

deltas.before: 需要为每个任务设计复杂的特征提取和分类流水线，涉及大量手工调优和任务特定训练。
deltas.after: 使用单一的、预训练的CNN模型提取通用特征，仅需训练一个简单的线性分类器。
deltas.why_it_matters: 极大地简化了视觉识别系统的构建流程，降低了任务特定设计和调优的成本，同时获得了与或优于专用系统相当的性能。

deltas.before: 特征表示通常维度较低（如几千维），且需要针对任务进行设计。
deltas.after: 使用高维（4096维）的深度CNN特征，这些特征在通用数据集上学习，具有强大的语义表达能力。
deltas.why_it_matters: 深度CNN特征能够捕获更丰富、更抽象的图像语义信息，从而在多种任务上表现出更好的泛化能力。

deltas.before: 对于细粒度识别和属性检测等任务，通常需要部件对齐、姿态归一化等复杂预处理。
deltas.after: 直接使用从整个对象边界框提取的全局CNN特征，无需复杂的部件对齐。
deltas.why_it_matters: 表明CNN特征本身具有一定的姿态不变性和部件感知能力，能够处理一定程度的形变和遮挡。

deltas.before: 图像检索方法通常需要在目标数据集上训练大型词典或编码（如Fisher向量），内存占用高。
deltas.after: 使用固定的CNN特征（4096维）进行检索，内存占用相对较低，且无需在目标数据集上训练。
deltas.why_it_matters: 提供了一种内存效率较高且无需任务特定训练的检索方案，在多个数据集上取得了有竞争力的结果。

variables.name: \text{layer 22}
variables.description: OverFeat网络的第一个全连接层

formulas.intuition: 将输入图像通过预训练的CNN前向传播，提取特定中间层的激活值作为图像的通用特征表示。
标准的铰链损失函数，用于训练线性SVM分类器，目标是找到最大间隔超平面将正负样本分开。
在图像检索中，计算查询子块与参考图像所有子块之间的最小L2距离，用于衡量局部相似性。

main_result.baseline_comparison: 优于所有使用外部训练数据的先前方法（如GHM: 64.7%, AGS: 71.1%, NUS: 70.5%）。
显著优于大多数非CNN基线（如IFV: 60.8%, MLrep: 64.0%），与专门为CNN特征设计的多尺度池化方法（68.9%）相当。
在不使用部件标注的情况下，性能接近使用部件标注的DPD（51.0%），并优于Poof（56.8%）。使用部件标注的DPD+CNN达到65.0%。
与使用部件标注的DPD（69.9%）性能相当，并显著优于Poselets（65.2%）。
优于大多数低内存占用方法（如BoW: 36.4%, VLAD: 55.5%），但低于使用大型词典的ASMK+MA（81.7%）。

ablation.description: 研究使用不同网络层提取的特征对分类性能的影响。
ablation.finding: 随着网络层加深，分类性能（mAP）总体呈上升趋势，但在ReLU层处会出现下降，因为半波整流丢失了信息。

ablation.description: 比较CNN-SVM（无增强）与CNNaug-SVM（有增强）的性能。
ablation.finding: 在所有任务上，数据增强（裁剪、旋转、幂变换）均能带来一致的性能提升。

robustness.description: 在从图像分类到属性检测、图像检索等多种逐渐偏离原始训练任务的任务上进行测试。
robustness.finding: CNN特征在所有测试任务上均表现出强大的泛化能力，性能一致优于或媲美专用方法。

scaling.finding: 4096维特征在多个任务上均有效，但论文未系统研究不同维度的影响。

case_study.description: 分析CNN-SVM在MIT-67数据集上的混淆矩阵。
case_study.finding: 混淆矩阵具有强对角线，表明分类准确。少数混淆的类别（如不同类型的商店）即使对人类来说也难以区分。

efficiency.finding: 大大减少了任务特定的计算开销和设计复杂度。

efficiency.finding: 相比训练复杂的专用模型（如DPM、多层表示），训练效率更高。

evidence.description: 在Pascal VOC 2007图像分类任务上，CNN-SVM达到73.9% mAP，CNNaug-SVM达到77.2% mAP，优于所有使用外部训练数据的先前方法。
在MIT-67场景识别任务上，CNN-SVM达到58.4%平均准确率，CNNaug-SVM达到69.0%，显著优于大多数非CNN基线。
在CUB 200-2011细粒度识别任务上，CNN-SVM达到53.3%平均准确率，CNNaug-SVM达到61.8%，在不使用部件标注的情况下性能接近使用部件标注的DPD。
在H3D属性检测任务上，CNN-SVM达到70.8% mAP，CNNaug-SVM达到73.0%，与使用部件标注的DPD性能相当。
在Oxford5k图像检索任务上，CNNaug-ss达到68.0% mAP，优于大多数低内存占用方法。

claims.claim: 简单的线性分类器（SVM）与CNN特征结合即可获得强大性能。
risk_flags: 未探索更复杂的分类器（如神经网络）是否能带来进一步提升。

evidence.description: 论文使用线性SVM作为分类器，在多个任务上获得强大性能，表明CNN特征本身已编码了丰富的语义信息。
在Pascal VOC 2007、MIT-67、CUB 200-2011、H3D等多个数据集上，线性SVM与CNN特征结合均获得有竞争力的结果。

evidence.description: 在所有任务上，CNNaug-SVM（有数据增强）均优于CNN-SVM（无数据增强），证明数据增强技术能带来一致的性能提升。
数据增强技术包括裁剪、旋转和分量幂变换，这些简单的技术即可提升性能。

terms.definition: 指直接使用在大型通用数据集（如ImageNet）上预训练的卷积神经网络作为特征提取器，而不针对特定任务进行微调。
一个用于图像分类、定位和检测的卷积神经网络架构，由Sermanet等人在2014年提出。本文使用其在ILSVRC13上预训练的大型版本。
从CNN特定层（如第一个全连接层）提取的激活值组成的向量，用作图像的表示。本文中为4096维。
支持向量机的一种，使用线性核函数。本文中用于对CNN特征进行分类。
通过对训练数据进行变换（如裁剪、旋转、缩放、颜色抖动等）来人工扩充数据集的技术，旨在提升模型的泛化能力和鲁棒性。
一种特征变换方法，对特征向量的每个维度进行幂运算（如平方）。本文中用于CNNaug-SVM设置。
平均精度均值，是信息检索和目标检测中常用的评估指标，计算所有查询（或类别）的平均精度的平均值。

steps.description: 1. 获取预训练的OverFeat网络模型（大型版本）。
2. 对于每个数据集，将图像调整为221×221像素。
3. 使用OverFeat网络提取第22层（第一个全连接层）的4096维特征向量。
4. 对特征向量进行L2归一化。
5. 对于分类任务（CNN-SVM），使用libsvm或liblinear训练线性SVM分类器。对于多类问题，采用一对一策略。
6. 对于增强版本（CNNaug-SVM），对训练数据进行增强：添加裁剪和旋转样本，并对特征进行分量幂变换（每个维度取平方）。
7. 对于图像检索任务，计算查询图像与数据库图像特征之间的L2距离。对于空间搜索，采用多尺度子块提取和最小距离聚合策略。
8. 在相应数据集上评估性能（使用mAP、平均准确率等指标）。

metadata.title: CNN Features Off-the-Shelf: An Astounding Baseline for Recognition
metadata.venue: 2014 IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops
metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / CNN / Computer Vision / Top-cited Computer Vision paper
metadata.abstract: Recent results indicate that the generic descriptors extracted from the convolutional neural networks are very powerful. This paper adds to the mounting evidence that this is indeed the case. We report on a series of experiments conducted for different recognition tasks using the publicly available code and model of the OverFeat network which was trained to perform object classification on ILSVRC13. We use features extracted from the OverFeat network as a generic image representation to tackle the diverse range of recognition tasks of object image classification, scene recognition, fine grained recognition, attribute detection and image retrieval applied to a diverse set of datasets. We selected these tasks and datasets as they gradually move further away from the original task and data the OverFeat network was trained to solve. Astonishingly, we report consistent superior results compared to the highly tuned state-of-the-art systems in all the visual classification tasks on various datasets. For instance retrieval it consistently outperforms low memory footprint methods except for sculptures dataset. The results are achieved using a linear SVM classifier (or L2 distance in case of retrieval) applied to a feature representation of size 4096 extracted from a layer in the net. The representations are further modified using simple augmentation techniques e.g. jittering. The results strongly suggest that features obtained from deep learning with convolutional nets should be the primary candidate in most visual recognition tasks.

But when the convolutional neural network OverFeat [38] was recently made pub- licly available 1 it allowed for some experimentation. In particular we wondered now, not whether one could train a deep network speciﬁcally for a given task, but if the fea- tures extracted by a deep network - one carefully trained on the diverse ImageNet database to perform the speciﬁc task of image classiﬁcation - could be exploited for a wide variety of vision tasks. We now relate our discussions and general ﬁndings because as a computer vision researcher you’ve probably had the same questions: Prof: First off has anybody else investigated this issue? Student: Well it turns out Donahue et al . [10], Zeiler and Fergus [48] and Oquab et al. [29]...

It would be fun to more thoroughly investigate how 1There are other publicly available deep learning implementations such as Alex Krizhevsky’s ConvNet and Berkeley’s Caffe. Prof: The simplest thing we could try is to extract an image feature vector from the OverFeat network and combine this with a simple linear classiﬁer. Student: Deﬁnitely image classiﬁcation . Several vision groups have already produced a big jump in performance from the previous sate-of-the-art methods on Pascal VOC. But maybe ﬁne-tuning the network was necessary for the jump? I’m going to try it on Pascal VOC and just to make it a little bit trickier the MIT scene dataset. Answer: OverFeat does a very good job even without ﬁne-tuning (section 3.2 for details). Prof: Okay so that result conﬁrmed previous ﬁndings and is perhaps not so surprising. (Section 3.4 for details.) Prof: Next challenge attribute detection? Let’s see if the OverFeat features have encoded something about the se- mantic properties of people and objects. Student: Do you think the global CNN features extracted from the person’s bounding box can cope with the articu- lations and occlusions present in the H3D dataset. All the best methods do some sort of part alignment before classi- ﬁcation and during training. Answer: Surprisingly the CNN features on average beat poselets and a deformable part model for the person at- tributes labelled in the H3D dataset. Wow, how did they do that?! They also work extremely well on the object at- tribute dataset. Maybe these OverFeat features do indeed encode attribute information? (Details in section 3.5.) Prof: Can we push things even further? network. It takes as input color images of size 221 ×221. Please consult [38] and [22] for further details. OverFeat was trained for the image classiﬁcation task of ImageNet ILSVRC 2013 [1] and obtained very competitive results for the classiﬁcation task of the 2013 challenge and won the localization task. ILSVRC13 contains 1.2 million images which are hand labelled with the presence/absence of 1000 categories. The images are mostly centered and the dataset is considered less challenging in terms of clutter and occlusion than other object recognition datasets such as PASCAL VOC [12]. We report results on a series of experiments we conducted on different recognition tasks. The tasks and datasets were selected such that they gradually move further away from the task the OverFeat network was trained to perform. We have two sections for visual classiﬁcation (Sec. 3) and visual instance retrieval (Sec. 4) where we review different tasks and datasets and report the ﬁnal results. The crucial

thing to remember is that the CNN features used are trained only using ImageNet data though the simple classiﬁers are trained using images speciﬁc to the task’s dataset. Finally, we have to point out that, given enough computa- tional resources, optimizing the CNN features for speciﬁc tasks/datasets would probably boost the performance of the simplistic system even further [29, 15, 51, 43, 41]. 3. Visual Classiﬁcation Here we go through different tasks related to visual classi- ﬁcation in the following subsections. 3.1. Method For all the experiments, unless stated otherwise, we use the ﬁrst fully connected layer (layer 22) of the network as our
feature vector. Note the max-pooling and rectiﬁcation oper-

ations are each considered as a separate layer inOverFeat which differs from Alex Krizhevsky’s ConvNet number- ing. For all the experiments we resize the whole image (or cropped sub-window) to 221×221. This gives a vector of 4096 dimensions. We have two settings: • The feature vector is further L2 normalized to unit length for all the experiments. We use the 4096 di- mensional feature vector in combination with a Sup- port Vector Machine (SVM) to solve different classiﬁ- cation tasks (CNN-SVM). • We further augment the training set by adding cropped and rotated samples and doing component- wise power transform and report separate results (CN- Naug+SVM). For the classiﬁcation scenarios where the labels are not mu- tually exclusive ( e.g. VOC Object Classiﬁcation or UIUC Object attributes) we use a one-against-all strategy, in the rest of experiments we use one-against-one linear SVMs with voting. Image Classiﬁcation To begin, we adopt the CNN representation to tackle the problem of image classiﬁcation of objects and scenes. The system should assign (potentially multiple) semantic labels to an image. Remember in contrast to object detection, ob- ject image classiﬁcation requires no localization of the ob- jects. The CNN representation has been optimized for the object image classiﬁcation task of ILSVRC. Therefore, in this experiment the representation is more aligned with the ﬁnal task than the rest of experiments. However, we have chosen two different image classiﬁcation datasets, objects and indoor scenes, whose image distributions differ from that of ILSVRC dataset.
3.2.1 Datasets

We use two challenging recognition datasets, Namely, Pas- cal VOC 2007 for object image classiﬁcation [12] and the MIT-67 indoor scenes [36] for scene recognition. Pascal VOC. Pascal VOC 2007 [12] contains∼10000 im- ages of 20 classes including animals, handmade and nat- ural objects. The objects are not centered and in general the appearance of objects in VOC is perceived to be more challenging than ILSVRC. Pascal VOC images come with bounding box annotation which are not used in our experi- ments. MIT-67 indoor scenes. The MIT scenes dataset has 15620 images of 67 indoor scene classes. The dataset consists of different types of stores ( e.g. bakery, grocery) residen- tial rooms (e.g. nursery room, bedroom), public spaces (e.g. inside bus, library, prison cell), leisure places ( e.g. buffet, fastfood, bar, movietheater) and working places ( e.g. of- ﬁce, operating room, tv studio). Fine grained Recognition Fine grained recognition has recentl...
to its huge potential for both commercial and cataloging
applications. Fine grained recognition is specially inter-

esting because it involves recognizing subclasses of the same object class such as different bird species, dog breeds, ﬂower types, etc. The advent of many new datasets with ﬁne-grained annotations such as Oxford ﬂowers [27], Cal- tech bird species [45], dog breeds [1], cooking activi- ties [37], cats and dogs [32] has helped the ﬁeld develop quickly. The subtlety of differences across different subor- dinate classes (as opposed to different categories) requires a ﬁne-detailed representation. This characteristic makes ﬁne- grained recognition a good test of whether a generic repre- sentation can capture these subtle details.
3.4.1 Datasets

We evaluate CNN features on two ﬁne-grained recognition datasets CUB 200-2011 and 102 Flowers. Caltech-UCSD Birds (CUB) 200-2011 dataset [45] is cho- sen since many recent methods have reported performance on it. It contains 11,788 images of 200 bird subordinates. 5994 images are used for training and 5794 for evaluation. Many of the species in the dataset exhibit extremely subtle differences which are sometimes even hard for humans to distinguish. Multiple levels of annotation are available for this dataset - bird bounding boxes, 15 part landmarks, 312 binary attributes and boundary segmentation. The majority of the methods applied use the bounding box and part land- marks for training. In this work we only use the bounding box annotation during training and testing. Oxford 102 ﬂowers dataset [27] contains 102 categories. Each category contains 40 to 258 of images. The ﬂowers appear at different scales, pose and lighting conditions.
